title: Expand More, Shrink Less: Shaping Effective-Rank Dynamics for Dense Scaling in Recommendation

problem.claim: Scaling recommendation models is challenging, and RankMixer suffers from embedding collapse that limits representation expressivity and underutilizes expanded representation space.

gap.claim: Rigid token mixing and P-FFN modules induce a damped oscillatory effective-rank trajectory across layers, motivating a more spectrum-robust architecture.

contributions.claim: RankElastor is an architecture designed to produce spectrum-robust representations with provable collapse mitigation.
Parameterized full mixing enables expressive token mixing with improved spectral robustness.
GLU-improved P-FFNs stabilize representation spectra through GLU-style feedforward modules.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present RankElastor as a novel architecture.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on large-scale industrial datasets consistently improve recommendation performance, mitigate embedding collapse, and exhibit robust scaling behavior.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scaling recommendation models is a central challenge.
RankMixer uses unified token representations with alternating token mixing and per-token feedforward networks for scalable performance.
RankMixer exhibits embedding collapse and a damped oscillatory effective-rank trajectory caused primarily by rigid token mixing and P-FFN modules.
RankElastor addresses collapse with parameterized full mixing and GLU-improved P-FFNs.
Experiments on large-scale industrial datasets report improved recommendation performance, reduced embedding collapse, and robust scaling behavior.

source_observation.claim: Rigid mixing and feedforward modules can jointly produce undesirable effective-rank dynamics across layers.

interpretation.claim: Monitoring representation-spectrum dynamics may reveal architectural causes of expressivity loss that aggregate performance metrics miss.

application.claim: Analyze effective-rank trajectories when diagnosing representation collapse in deep recommendation architectures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that effective-rank dynamics are the dominant failure mechanism for other model families or tasks.

source_observation.claim: The proposed architecture combines spectral-robust token mixing with GLU-style feedforward modules.

interpretation.claim: Addressing representation collapse may require coordinated changes across interacting architectural modules.

application.claim: Evaluate coupled architectural modifications when independent module changes jointly shape representation spectra.

exception.claim: The abstract does not identify which component contributes most to the reported improvements.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, model scales, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical analysis or the claimed collapse-mitigation proof.
The abstract does not establish results beyond the reported large-scale industrial experiments.
